reason: I want to eat from the garden, and harvesting the lettuce is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect to cut some lettuce leaves that can then be prepared at the galley.

effect: The harvest produced lettuce leaves, which I can now take to the galley.
reaction: The result was straightforward; I’m curious how the meal will fit into the long storm.
reason: Using the leaves at the galley seems like the next step toward eating from the garden.
expectation: I expect to prepare or eat the lettuce and complete the goal.

alternatives.reason: I considered harvesting again, but I already have leaves to prepare.

effect: The galley action completed the garden meal and the chapter.
reaction: The detail of sending Mara a message with the first crunch in it made the quiet meal feel personal.

mostWorthwhile.text: Preparing the supper was most worthwhile: it connected the garden's survival to a small, tangible moment during the storm.

leastWorthwhile.text: Harvesting the leaves was straightforward and produced no further detail on its own.

surprise.text: The voice message with the first crunch was a pleasing detail I hadn't anticipated.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary; harvesting lettuce and taking it to the galley followed naturally from the goal.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the storm ends and what happens to the specimens, although this chapter offered little gameplay choice.
